title: The Exodar
body: The Exodar was never meant to be a city. It was a dimensional ship, a satellite of Tempest Keep, the fortress the naaru brought to the Netherstorm of Outland. When Prince Kael'thas and his blood elves seized the keep and captured the naaru M'uru, the naaru O'ros barred them from its own section and hid within the vessel. Prophet Velen led a raid to take it and flee in search of allies on Azeroth, but the voyage ended in disaster. The ship came down on the western side of Azuremyst Isle, crashing into the flank of a mountain, and its survivors cannot say why. The draenei made its largest surviving section their capital. Its heart is the round Seat of the Naaru, where O'ros still dwells, and from it branch the Crystal Hall of the shaman, the Vault of Lights where Velen keeps his court, and the busy Trader's Tier. Elekks wait outside the entrance, and from a dock below the western wall ships sail to Auberdine, the nearest town of the Alliance the draenei have joined.

title: Seat of the Naaru
body: At the center of the Exodar lies the Seat of the Naaru, a great round hall with a shimmer of purple light at its heart. On its lowest level dwells the naaru O'ros. Around the rim open the bank and the auction house, and the city's peacekeepers greet visitors with the blessings of the naaru. Herald Bran'daan cries the latest news from both continents, from the Plaguelands to Feathermoon Stronghold. Off the spiral ramp of the main entrance, Caregiver Breel keeps the inn called the Exobar. Not all of the ship survived: two artificers stand before a district ruined in the crash, and from time to time the great hull still shudders.

title: The Crystal Hall
body: The Crystal Hall forms the northern wing of the Exodar, a quiet place built around a shining pool known as the Light Blessed Waters. It belongs to the shaman. Farseer Nobundo teaches here with Sulaa, Gurrag and Hobahken, who bid their pupils respect the elements of this world and the balance its spirits keep. Seer Skaltesh, guide to the shaman seeking enlightenment, offers even those on other paths a draught of elemental sapta, and with it they glimpse the many elemental spirits that share the hall unseen. Broken miners work a small cavern of crystal off to one side. Enchanters and jewelcrafters teach their trades nearby.

title: The Vault of Lights
body: The Vault of Lights, the Exodar's western wing, is a house of the Light and of learning; a spiral walkway climbs from it to a second entrance above Valaar's Berth. Paladins train with Jol in the glowing Vindicators' Sanctum; priests gather in the Anchorites' Sanctum and mages in the Hall of the Mystics. Holographic emitters run a museum of the Burning Legion, naming each servant of the enemy for passing tour groups, down to the eredar, once the draenei's own noble kinsmen. Prophet Velen keeps to the upper platform under the watch of his guards, the Shield of Velen.

title: Trader's Tier
body: The Trader's Tier, the southern wing of the Exodar, holds most of the city's craftsmen and merchants. Smiths, engineers, leatherworkers and tailors keep their corners, and vendors sell weapons and armor of every weight. The ship's stores are thin. Dugiru, the cloth quartermaster, warns that the Exodar's once vast supply of textiles has dwindled dangerously low, and asks friends of the draenei for donations. Up the stairs lies the Hunters' Sanctum, where Ganaar passes on what he learned from the furbolgs about caring for beasts. At the top of a ramp, the highest point of the tier, warriors train on the Ring of Arms, where Behomat hands the little salvaged from the wreckage to those most able to use it.

title: Prophet Velen
body: Prophet Velen leads the draenei. On Argus he ruled the eredar beside Kil'jaeden and Archimonde, and when Sargeras offered them power, a vision showed Velen the price: worlds destroyed and his people turned to demons. He fled with those who would follow, and the Burning Legion has hunted the draenei ever since and found them even on Draenor, where the corrupted orcs slaughtered them. Now he holds court in the Vault of Lights. As his people seek this world's help against the Legion, he reminds them that they must also learn to live peaceably among its peoples. He welcomes the Broken as well, and calls the shamanism they teach critical to the draenei's future.

title: O'ros
body: O'ros is the naaru who came to Azeroth with the draenei and dwells deep in the Seat of the Naaru. With A'dal and M'uru it brought Tempest Keep to the Netherstorm. When Kael'thas Sunstrider's blood elves took the keep and captured M'uru, O'ros barred them from its own section and hid within the vessel that became the Exodar. The draenei hold it dear enough that one exarch swears by its beardless, geometric head.

title: Farseer Nobundo
body: Farseer Nobundo was a vindicator of Draenor until the orcs' fel magic twisted him into one of the Broken and cut him off from the Light. He went on pilgrimage to learn why and waited decades by an oasis for an answer that never came. Then a wind rose that would not stop, and in its voice he learned the truth: the Light had not forsaken the Broken, and the elements offered another path. When he came home, Velen, who had foreseen it, asked him to lead the Broken and teach shamanism to all. Many still despise the Broken or call the shaman's way blasphemy; Nobundo asks his pupils not to judge the flame by its outward appearance, nor him.

title: Torallius and Aalun
body: Outside the Exodar's entrance, the elekk pens belong to Torallius the Pack Handler, a one-eyed breeder of the great beasts the draenei brought from Draenor. He trusts no outsider with his elekks until they prove their friendship to his people. When Exarch Menelaous sends him promising youngsters with orders for the front on Bloodmyst Isle, he asks whether this is the best the Hand of Argus can do and swears the newcomer will never make it, then sends them on anyway. Beside him the riding trainer Aalun offers to teach the riding of the finest beasts anyone has seen, for a price, but not to outsiders the draenei do not hold in the highest esteem.

title: Huntress Kella Nightbow
body: Huntress Kella Nightbow is a night elf who keeps watch near Valaar's Berth, west of the Exodar, and every young draenei hunter is sent to her to learn the taming of beasts. Her method comes from the Stillpine furbolgs, who carve totems in the likeness of an animal that let a hunter bond with such a creature for a time. Her pupils begin with the feisty barbed crawlers of the western coast, move on to the greater timberstriders of the north and finish with a nightstalker.

parts.body: This pupil learned faster than Kella had imagined. She joked that the timberstrider had not pecked their eyes out, not that she ever thought it would, and once the nightstalker had hunted at their side she put away her last totem, carved in the likeness of a winged lizard she could not even name, and let them tame beasts on their own. Then she sent them to Ganaar in the Trader's Tier.

title: The Draenei Call of Water
body: When a draenei shaman has grown in wisdom, Farseer Nobundo calls them back to the Crystal Hall to learn the mysteries of water. A powerful water elemental, Aqueous, has asked for help: something is throwing the waters of Bloodmyst Isle out of balance, and Nobundo is not surprised, given the blood elves' unnatural ways. With a potion to help them reach her, the shaman finds Aqueous in a hidden reef beneath the waves off the island's northern shore, where she speaks with them mind to mind. A great disturbance is fouling the waters on and around the isle, plain to see in its creatures. Water gives life, she teaches, yet polluted it brings life to an end, and she would learn how far the harm runs from the essences of her unfortunate sisters, the spirits of the Foul Pool.
sources: quests 9500, 9502, 10490 (Sulaa, Farseer Javad in Ironforge, Farseer Umbrua in Stormwind send the shaman to Nobundo)
quest 9501 description and reward text (Aqueous, imbalance on Bloodmyst, blood elves' unnatural predilections, potion, hidden reef off the northern shore, speaking with minds)

quests 9508, 9509 (Tel'athion the Impure's demented research, destroy the barrels, flask of purest water held back, Nobundo makes the water totem)
notes: Converted: the opening keeps the call, Aqueous's request and her reef, and the Foul Pool errand (quests 9500, 9501 description and reward, 9503 description). The corruption's reach moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 9504, whose description tells it; 9503's reward does not); Tel'athion as the source to part 2 (QUEST_ACCEPT 9508, which needs 9504 turned in, so its reward line is also seen); his end to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 9508); the flask and the water totem to part 4 (QUEST_DONE 9509). KILL on Tel'athion is not used (left to Bloodmyst's Foul Pool entry). Before: Ownership: the chain starts and ends with Nobundo in the Exodar but plays out on Bloodmyst (Hidden Reef 3596, Foul Pool 3595, Tel'athion's Camp 3603); told here as a story, so Bloodmyst should not retell it or use 9500-9509/10490 but may write those places and Tel'athion as a KILL. The source of the pure water is contradictory in the DB (9504: naga ruins on this island; 9508, 9509: from Ashenvale), so it is left unnamed. Faction 1: 9500, 9501 and 10490 are draenei only; 9502 has no race limit but its giver Farseer Javad 23127 (Ironforge) is template 1638, hostile to the Horde; 10490's giver Farseer Umbrua 20407 (Stormwind) is template 1640. Fact-check: givers and enders verified (Sulaa, Javad, Umbrua to Nobundo; 9501 Nobundo to Aqueous; 9509 Aqueous back to Nobundo), so the chain is the Exodar's. Javad and Umbrua are not used by ironforge.json or stormwind.json. Check: part 4 reworded: Aqueous gives the shaman the flask to take to Nobundo (9509 description); she does not send it herself. ACCEPT triggers verified: 9504 and 9508 are QuestType 2 without the auto-complete flag and are each offered by Aqueous right after the previous turn-in (9503 and 9504 RewardNextQuest).

parts.body: The essences showed the corruption was worse than Aqueous had feared, so potent that, left unchecked, it could spread to the ocean currents and be carried throughout all of Azeroth. Only water of the greatest purity could counter it, and she sent the shaman to gather some.
sources: quest 9504 description (worse than I feared, corruption could spread to the ocean currents throughout Azeroth, sample of the purest water)

parts.body: Water parts easily, Aqueous teaches, yet put enough of it together and it becomes an unstoppable force, and she and the shaman are that force, not those who poisoned the isle. She has found the source: a small camp southwest of the Foul Pool, where Tel'athion the Impure carries on demented research whose filth seeps into the island's water. Pure water poured over his barrels will draw him out.
sources: quest 9504 reward text (water parts easily, an unstoppable force, not those that have poisoned Bloodmyst)
quest 9508 description (corruption the by-product of demented research, Tel'athion the Impure's camp southwest of the Foul Pool, destroy his cache of barrels with the pure water to bring him out)

parts.body: Tel'athion fell, and with him the crisis passed. The restoration of the island's water has begun, and in time, with the other elements, it will heal itself. Aqueous only wishes the blood elves could see that in fouling their surroundings they are killing themselves as well.
sources: quest 9508 log text (bring the head of Tel'athion) and reward text (crisis averted, restoration in motion, the water will heal itself, the blood elves killing themselves)

parts.body: Aqueous had held back a little of the pure water, not from doubt but because she knew the shaman would succeed, and gave it to them in a flask to carry back to Nobundo. The elements had already told the farseer of the shaman's deeds, and he bound the water's essence into a powerful water totem.
sources: quest 9509 description (held back a little of the water, knew you would succeed, flask of pure water, a very powerful water totem), completion and reward text (the elements have spoken of your deeds, combine its essence into your new water totem)

title: The Draenei Call of Air
body: Air is the last of the four elements a draenei shaman comes to know, and Farseer Nobundo calls only those wise enough to go on. He sends them up the Wildwind Path on the northern face of the very mountain the Exodar crashed into. In a cave at its peak lives Velaada, one of his most accomplished pupils, who sees few visitors and heard of this one's coming on the wind. Air seems ethereal, she teaches, yet fills everything: her cave's rocks are mostly air, the oceans are saturated with it, and no fire burns without it, though the other elements had best not hear her say so. True wisdom waits with Susurrus, a lord of the winds, at the northern edge of the precipice.
sources: quests 9551, 9547, 10491 (Sulaa, Farseer Javad, Farseer Umbrua: the last of the elements)

quest 9552 description and reward text (Wildwind Path on the north facing of the mountain the Exodar crashed into, cave at its peak, Velaada one of Nobundo's most accomplished pupils, whispered on the winds)
npc_text 8956 (Velaada: so few visitors up here)
quest 9553 description (air permeates everything, rocks mostly air, oceans saturated, fire cannot be sustained, don't let those elements hear; Susurrus at the northern edge of the precipice)

quest 9554 description, request and reward text (no further task, atone for the ship falling from my skies, portion of my being, fly you back down, hair looks ruffled, Nobundo grins, whorl into the air totem)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Wildwind_Peak (Susurrus, lord of the air elementals in the region)
notes: Converted: the opening keeps the call, the climb, Velaada and her teaching, and Susurrus waiting (quests 9551, 9552, 9553 descriptions). Susurrus's judgment and gift moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 9554, whose description tells it); the return and the air totem to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 9554). Dialogue check: npc_text 8956 holds nothing from later builds. Before: Plays out on Wildwind Peak (3580), which Azuremyst skipped; no AREA trigger since the city's halls also map to 3580/3581. 9552 is listed because it has no prerequisite. Faction 1: all draenei only. 14111 (Relic of the Earthen Ring, Ironforge) not used. Fact-check: verified 9551, 9547, 10491 end at Nobundo; 9552 runs to Velaada, 9553 to Susurrus, 9554 back to Nobundo; azuremyst.json has no Wildwind Peak, Velaada or Susurrus entry. 9547 and 9551 are draenei only. Check: ACCEPT 9554 verified: QuestType 2, not auto-complete, offered by Susurrus right after 9553 (RewardNextQuest); the whole reveal is in its description.

parts.body: Unlike his brothers and sisters of the other elements, Susurrus asked no task. The shaman had done enough, he judged, to atone for the ship that fell to this place from his skies, and already held the wisdom to use air well. He gave a portion of his own being to carry back to Nobundo, and offered to fly the shaman back down to the Exodar.
sources: quest 9553 reward text (Susurrus: you come seeking wisdom)
quest 9554 description (no further task, atone for the ship falling from my skies, portion of my being, fly you back down to the Exodar)

parts.body: Back in the Crystal Hall, Nobundo grinned at the shaman's ruffled hair. Proud of a pupil who had persevered where others falter, he took the whorl from Susurrus and shaped it into an air totem, both a focus and a reminder of the bond forged with the elements.
sources: quest 9554 completion text (your hair looks ruffled, Nobundo grins knowingly) and reward text (persevered where others falter, imbue the whorl into your air totem, a focus and a reminder)

title: Redemption
body: At Azure Watch, the paladin Tullas admits that even he at times struggles to follow the path of the Light, and he sends his best pupils to his own teacher, Jol, in the Vindicators' Sanctum, a room of the Vault of Lights wrapped in a vibrant glow. Jol's charge is to set paladins on the way to greater virtue as they devote themselves to the Light and defend their people from every threat. Her first lesson is a tome of divinity, to be studied and understood, for only those who understand what the Light expects of them, and are capable, will attain greater abilities.
sources: quest 10366 description and reward text (Tullas: even I struggle; Jol trained me; Vindicators' Sanctum, a room surrounded by a vibrant glow of light)
quest 9598 description and reward text (putting paladins on the path to greater virtue, tome of divinity, acts of compassion in the wake of the crash)

quest 9600 description, request and reward text (young Stillpine shaman slaughtered at a Bristlelimb camp after the bridge, Symbol of Life, all life is worth saving if it does not oppose us, bewilderment of the revived)
DB: Tullas 17483 at Azure Watch (3576); Young Furbolg Shaman 17542 in Bristlelimb Enclave (3600)
notes: Converted: the opening keeps Tullas's breadcrumb, Jol's charge and the tome (quests 10366, 9598 descriptions). The furbolg test moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 9600, which needs 9598 turned in, so its reward line is also seen); the revived shaman, Jol's lesson and the new power to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 9600). Before: Ownership: starts and ends with Jol in the Exodar; only the middle step is at Bristlelimb Enclave on Bloodmyst (3600), so Bloodmyst should not use 9598/9600/10366. 10366 is the Azure Watch breadcrumb, 9598 the true first step. Faction 1: all draenei only. Fact-check: verified 10366 Tullas (Azure Watch) to Jol 17509 in the Vindicators' Sanctum (-4192,-11472); 9598 and 9600 both start and end at Jol; azuremyst.json does not use Tullas or 10366. Check: 'from its threats' (read as the Light's) changed to 'from every threat' (9598 description). ACCEPT 9600 verified: QuestType 2, not auto-complete, offered by Jol right after 9598 (RewardNextQuest).

parts.body: Then comes a test of compassion, for in the wake of the Exodar's crash there are always people in need of help. Several young Stillpine shaman, allies of the draenei, stumbled on a Bristlelimb camp just past the bridge to Bloodmyst Isle and were slaughtered to the last. With a Symbol of Life the paladin is to raise one of them from death.
sources: quest 9598 reward text (tasks in the wake of the Exodar's crash, acts of compassion, people who need help)
quest 9600 description (young Stillpine shaman slaughtered at a Bristlelimb camp after the bridge, Symbol of Life, resurrect one)

parts.body: The young furbolg woke bewildered, as anyone would who returns to the world of the living to find a strange being standing over them. All life is worth saving if it does not oppose us, Jol teaches; only enemies should be laid to rest for good. The power to call back the fallen is the paladin's from then on.
sources: quest 9600 completion text (all life is worth saving, if it does not oppose us) and reward text (bewilderment of the revived, a strange being, you may call upon this power)
